What is Trading Tracker 2026 & How Does It Empower Traders?

The institutional-grade trading journal and mathematical discipline engine engineered to transform emotional retail trading into consistent profitability.

1. Precision Multi-Asset Journaling

Log Indian Equities, Index Options (NIFTY, BANKNIFTY, FINNIFTY, SENSEX), Futures, Forex, and Crypto trades with custom setup tags, stop-loss metrics, and chart screenshots.

❓ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Is Trading Tracker 2026 suitable for Indian stock and options traders?

Yes, Trading Tracker 2026 is fully tailored for Indian traders tracking NIFTY, BANKNIFTY, SENSEX, and MCX commodities, supporting INR (₹) formatting, CE/PE call tags, and brokerage calculations.

Is my trade data secure and confidential?

Absolutely. All journal logs are stored client-side in your private browser sandbox with 256-bit encryption. You can export encrypted JSON backups or erase your logs whenever you choose.

Does Trading Tracker offer advisory calls or stock tips?

No. Trading Tracker 2026 is an analytical software tool for personal trade evaluation and educational discipline. We are not a SEBI-registered advisor and do not offer investment tips.

⚠️ SEBI Regulatory Risk Warning: Derivative trading (Futures & Options) carries high market risk. As per SEBI studies, 9 out of 10 individual traders incur net financial losses. Please trade responsibly with strict risk management.

📚 Pro Trading Knowledge Hub & Masterclass

Practical rules, price action setups, option buying strategies & psychology guide by Anurag Patel
🚀 1. High Probability Breakout + Volume Confirmation
  • Entry Rule: Never enter blindly on candle touch. Wait for a 5-minute candle to close completely above resistance with volume higher than the 20-period average.
  • Stop-Loss: Strictly placed below the breakout candle's low or nearest swing low.
  • Target: Minimum 1:2 Risk-to-Reward ratio or next major daily resistance level.
🔄 2. Support & Resistance Pullback / Retest Setup
  • Concept: Old resistance becomes new support after a breakout. Institutional traders buy on the retest.
  • Entry Trigger: Look for a bullish rejection candle (Hammer / Bullish Engulfing) when price retests the broken zone.
  • Advantage: Offers the smallest stop-loss and highest risk-to-reward ratio (often 1:3 to 1:5).
🪤 3. Trap & Fakeout Avoidance Rule
  • If a candle breaks a key high/low with a long wick and closes back inside the consolidation range, it is an institutional trap.
  • Action: If you were in the trade, exit immediately without waiting for Stop Loss. Never hope or average losing trades.
🎯 1. Strike Price Selection: Strictly ATM / In-The-Money (ITM)
  • Delta Rule: Always buy At-The-Money (ATM, Delta ~0.50) or slightly In-The-Money (ITM, Delta 0.55-0.70).
  • Avoid Out-Of-The-Money (OTM): Cheap ₹10-₹20 OTM options lose 80% value due to theta decay even if market goes sideways. Cheap options are the #1 reason 90% buyers lose money.
⚡ 2. Expiry Day Hero-or-Zero Strict Protocol
  • Hero-or-Zero capital allocation should NEVER exceed 2% of your account capital.
  • Enter only after 1:30 PM when 15-minute range breakout occurs with high momentum.
  • Treat this amount as 100% risk — if trade goes against you, exit without emotion.
📊 3. India VIX & Premium Volatility Factor
  • VIX > 15: High volatility — fast premium expansion. Keep wider targets.
  • VIX < 12: Low volatility — slow premium movement and high decay. Prefer quick scalping.
🛑 1. The 2-Trade Daily Loss Lock (Anti-Revenge Rule)
  • If you take 2 consecutive losses in a day, immediately close your trading terminal.
  • Revenge trading to "recover" morning losses always leads to devastating capital wipeouts. Tomorrow is always another trading day.
🧘 2. Conquering FOMO (Fear Of Missing Out)
  • If you miss a 100-point rally candle, DO NOT chase at the top. Most retail buyers enter right where institutions take profit.
  • The market gives 3 to 5 high-probability setups every single day. Wait patiently for your specific setup.
💼 3. Red Days are Business Expenses
  • Every business has operational costs (electricity, rent, inventory). In trading, a disciplined small stop-loss is your business cost. Accept small losses gracefully.
🛡️ 1. The 1% - 2% Capital Risk Formula
  • Never risk more than 1% to 2% of your total account capital on a single trade.
  • Example: If capital is ₹50,000, max risk per trade is strictly ₹500 - ₹1,000.
  • Position Size: Quantity = (Max ₹ Risk) ÷ (Entry Price - Stop Loss).
⚖️ 2. Mandatory Minimum 1:2 Risk-to-Reward Ratio
  • If your risk is 15 points (₹1,000), your target must be at least 30 points (₹2,000).
  • With a 1:2 R:R, even with only 40% win rate, you will consistently make net profits!
📈 3. Capital Scaling Rule
  • Increase lot size ONLY after 20 consecutive profitable trading days in your journal, never after just 1 lucky day.
⚠️ 09:15 - 09:30 AM: Opening Volatility & Trap Zone

Institutional order matching & high bid-ask spread. Beginners should observe and mark the 15-min Opening Range (High & Low) rather than gambling on the first candle.

🔥 09:45 - 11:15 AM: Prime Momentum & Trend Window

The best trading window of the day. Clean breakouts, solid volume, and clear direction. 80% of daily target should be completed here.

😴 11:30 AM - 01:15 PM: Sideways Lunch Chop Zone

Market consolidates. Premiums decay rapidly. Avoid active option buying in this window to prevent giving back morning profits.

🚀 01:30 - 03:00 PM: Afternoon Trend Continuation / Reversal

European market opening brings fresh volume. Ideal for sharp expiry moves and trend continuation breakout trades.

🌅 Pre-Market Routine (08:30 - 09:15 AM)
  • Check Gift Nifty, Asian markets, and major news announcements.
  • Mark Key Levels on chart: Previous Day High (PDH), Previous Day Low (PDL), Previous Day Close (PDC), and major Weekly support/resistance.
  • Pre-define Today's Max Allowed Daily Loss (e.g. ₹2,000) before placing the first order.
🌇 Post-Market Routine (03:30 - 04:30 PM)
  • Log all trades immediately into Trading Tracker 2026 with entry reason, emotion, and screenshot.
  • Check if your Stop-Loss discipline score is 100%.
  • Review your mistakes without guilt and write 1 improvement lesson for tomorrow.
